theorem_C004D_1.statement: For a connected undirected unweighted graph with L=D-A: the symmetric heat generator -L has uniform stationary distribution P_uniform=1/N (since ker(L)=span{1}). The continuous-time random-walk generator Q=-D^{-1}L, uniquely determined (up to overall rate) as the reversible chain supported on the graph's own edges and detail-balanced w.r.t. P_ss=d/(2|E|) -- the condition BRIDGE B-005 itself invokes -- has degree-weighted stationary distribution P_ss=d/(2|E|). Its adjoint is Q*=Q^T=-LD^{-1}. Furthermore L_norm=D^{-1/2}LD^{-1/2} is similar to -Q via L_norm=D^{1/2}(-Q)D^{-1/2}, so Spec(-Q)=Spec(L_norm). For irregular graphs (not all degrees equal), Spec(L) != Spec(L_norm) in general, and Q != -L, Q* != -L.
theorem_C004D_1.status: PROVEN (algebraically, and independently verified numerically for G0-G4)

textual_inconsistency_found.claim_A: 'The generator is -L for the continuous-time random walk.' (54_SOURCE_TEXT_CORPUS row 2024, Markov Semigroup entry, uncertified descriptive text)
textual_inconsistency_found.claim_B: BRIDGE B-005 (CERTIFIED): stationary measure of the Fokker-Planck operator L* associated to the graph Laplacian is P_ss(i)=d_i/(2|E|), proved via Perron-Frobenius on 'the transition matrix' and 'the detailed balance condition'. (rows 1954-1957, confirmed again row 2137)
textual_inconsistency_found.resolution: Claims A and B coincide only for regular graphs (D=dI, a scalar multiple of I). For irregular graphs they are mathematically incompatible under a single operator -L: ker(L)=span{1} forces -L's stationary state to be uniform, contradicting B-005's own certified degree-weighted P_ss. B-005's own proof cites 'the transition matrix' and 'detailed balance' -- concepts that only pin down a unique operator (Q=-D^{-1}L, Q*=-LD^{-1}) once worked through explicitly, which this run does (Section 5 derivation). Recorded as GAP-GENERATOR-001, now resolved at the discrete level.

random_walk_generator_derivation.input: Graph edges A_ij in {0,1}; degree matrix D; detailed-balance condition (source: BRIDGE B-005's own proof sketch); target stationary measure P_ss=d/(2|E|) (source: BRIDGE B-005 CERTIFIED statement)
random_walk_generator_derivation.derivation: Detailed balance: pi_i*Lambda_ij = pi_j*Lambda_ji. Impose pi=P_ss=d/(2|E|). The unique rate law supported on the graph's own edges with no extra free parameters is Lambda_ij=A_ij/d_i (verified: (d_i/2E)(A_ij/d_i)=A_ij/2E=A_ji/2E=(d_j/2E)(A_ji/d_j) since A is symmetric). This gives Lambda=D^{-1}A-I=-D^{-1}(D-A)=-D^{-1}L=Q. Forward/adjoint operator on probability vectors: Q*=Q^T=-LD^{-1}.
random_walk_generator_derivation.status: DERIVED -- not imported from an external framework; built entirely from A, D, L, and B-005's own invoked detailed-balance condition.

continuum_correspondence.question: Is Q*=-LD^{-1} the discrete realization of the registered continuum expression L*P=-div(P*grad(log P_ss))?
continuum_correspondence.finding: Q* is the master-equation generator of the unique detailed-balanced reversible chain compatible with the graph's edges and P_ss -- the standard discrete form associated with reversible master equations. Literal convergence of this discrete operator to the specific continuum differential expression under mesh refinement is a separate discrete-to-continuum limit statement, not proved here and not resolved anywhere in the corpus (the analogous heat-kernel-to-geometry limit, BRIDGE B-004, is itself independently registered OPEN in source).
